the flames up the gangway. His shirt was burned

The flames increased and Reel given up for lost

The Garden City was pushed into her slip by

--Frascati, the Austrian drunkard, the
divorced husband on one side Of the
former wife; John Saunders, the lover
who had grown sick with longing for
face now not twenty feet away-yet

ence. Driven no doubt to despair by

Correspondence of THE EVENING STAR.


SARATOGA SPRINGS, October L. 1888


Aftermath! Yes, the full harvest has passed;
the hives silent, for the bees have swarmed, and
this lovely village is again settling down to its
normal condition. 1t is now the supplement
season. We have with us those who have been
enjoying lake, mountain and pastoral scenery,
but think their outings is not complete without
taste of these waters and a sight of this
famous place in its autumnal glory. The land
lords Of the large hotels have closed their doors
with sardOnic smiles, for this has not been a
flush year'with them. The profits do not half
equal those of last year. Even at the best it
takes little more each season to satisfy greedy
human nature, and hotel proprietorS are not
noted as exceptions, nor are they sentimental
people Bleeding pockets and hearts are the
same to them. When you gaze upon these
silent, grim caravanseries you cannot help
peOpling them in imagination and hearing the
sepulchral echo of the vanished football In fact
you become haunted with scenes and sounds
that, like BanquO's ghost, Twill not down."
yelled so completely by comedy that no one has
seen the dagger thrusts, and there is vet Emusic
in the air." Congress Park has done pretty well
during the season. 1t cleared forty Thousand
dollars, which goes to the liquidation Of the
debt upon the property, but allows no dividend
to stockholders this year.


new feature OF summer life at Saratoga was
the art gallery established this season. near the
park, In which was displayed some fine paint
ings. The proprietor realized ten per cent
from admission fees on his investment in build
ing and paintings, and sold many of the latter at
high prices. Both art and trade has been liber-
ally patrOEiZed. and many more baZaars have
been opened than heretofore.


The weather is delightful. There are many
here yet in the quiet restful hooks. Our tran
sient home is a perfect oasis around which fond
memories will always cling, as the many who
have found rest for mind and cure for bodily ills
can truly testify. There is peculiar charm in
being where you can feel perfectly at home, have
entertaining, cultured society, and an able ply
stefan to keep in order the frail mechanism of
the human body. Sanitariums, such as are
found here. are increasing in popularity. They
are generally perfect in their arrangement for
the comfort of guests, and afford means for bath
ing and exercise, while the prices reasonable.
The guests are always planning entertainments
excursions and various ways for filing IN the odd
moments so that time passes by so swiftly you
are surprised when you find the shadows deep
ening and the day closes but to bring us together
for the evenings pleasures.


Saratoga can now be thoroughly appreciated
for herself. The foliage is gorgeously beautiful,
the drives free from dust, carriage hire reasOna-

us-long since discovered that carelessness

Two hundred thousand dozen eggs have been
received at this port from Europe during the
past nine months. The importatons have
ceased until the middle Of September, when
they will be resumed. The home supply is so
large during the summer months and the risk
on imported eggs so great that for the ensuing
three months none will be brought from the
other side to place on the market here There
are only two houses here that import eggs The
firm Of John c. Mahr i Sons, at Washington
and Reade streets began receiving three years
ago, and the consignments to it have steadily
increased. The head of the house said yester-
day that the eggs that came TO this country
were shipped from Germany and Denmark prin-
cipa!ly, and also from France. Italy and Turkey
were two great egC-prOducing countries but
the shipments TO the United states were not
made from them. The eggs came packed in
straw in long cases containing 100 dozen each.
The only difference between imported eggs and
those produced in this country was that the
former were somewhat smaller and the shells
perhaps trife harder. The eggs were con-
signed on commission, aud the market here
Fixed their price They were sold at from / to
cents less per dozen than domestic eggs. The
lower price was on account of the size. and not
because they We're inferior in quality, for such
was not the case,


At this season Of the year. the dealer con.
tlnued. eggs were received fresh. During the
winter they came lined. That is they were
subjected to sort Of picking process in lime
water. The effect was to close the pores of the
shells, 80 that when boiled thev were apt to
break but not tenure the contents. Coming
from colder countries. the eggs kept better than
those laid here. This was true Of those brought
from Canada, and many were shipped from the
Dominion to the United States. The largest
reproducing states Of the Union were Ohio.
Indiana, and Iowa The breakage on imported
eggs was less than on those that came from the
west. They were transported by water and
were subjected to much violence. The impor-
tations had the effect of lowering prices here.
1t was when prices were high that the great
pront was made on imported eggs. A large
sale had been found for the eggs in Connecticut
and Massachusetts,. Whether retail dealers
told their customers that they were buying i'm
ported eggs the speaker could not say but he
saw no reason why any discrimination should
be made. The dealer that shipped to his firm
began sending to London drst- The surplus Of
81. ply intended for that market was sent to
this country, thus introducing the eggs here.
The outlook for the trade In the fall and winter
was good.


member Of another house in the general
produce trade said that In time eggs would
doubtless be sent from China to San Francisco
Poultry raising was an extensive industry Ia
China Eggs would keep as long as six or eight
months, although that was, Of course too long
and there were no difficulties about Transports
tion In the way. The cheapness with which
eggs could be produced in China made such q
thing possible. Fowls were kept on the boats

eggs could be sent from China to supply the
whole United States.

"Mam-ma1n! Mam-nlaml'" the baby cries,
Pointing his finger, dimpled and small,
To pictured face upon the wall.
With the softest, gentlest eyes,
The face OF the mother who gave him birth,
But who lieth alone In her narrow grave,
Buried beneath the cold, cold earth,


Where autumn grasses wave.
10000! oo-oow the darling COOS,


AS he lays his face on the senseless glass
But the fair head lying beneath the grass
Wet by the autumn dews
Can hear no sound from these baby lips
AS the days, and weeks, and months 20 on.
Her ear is dulled by dark eclipse,


And her eye is shut from the dawn.
All, little darling! the time will come


When your heart will long for single word
From the voice that may nevermore be heard
In her happy earthly home.
But afar away In the shining skies


am sure that her spirit will watch for you:
That the love still lives in those soft brown eyes
Above yon ether blue.
For the love OF a mother for her child
Is an essence that surely cannot die,
While the stars shall beam In the evening sky
Or roses bloom in the wild.
And, guarding ever your future way,
And lowering over your cradle bed,
May her blessing fall by night and day,
Upon your fair young head!
Christmas Eve, 1888.

slon;"

l see that one of those industrious German
writer's, always hunting the why's and where
fores OF things in general, has discovered the
origin of the word album" The writer points
out that in the middle ages the parchment in
common use was of two kinds-the Spanish
Italian and the German-French-and that the
main difference between these varieties lay in
the method of their preparation. The German
French could be written upon on both sides,
face was available. The smooth, white side of
this latter was called ''album," to distinguish
it from the stained exterior; and as the Spanish
Italian parchment, being stOuter and cheaper
than the other, was generally used for volumes
intended as repositories for scraps and literary
collections, the meaning of the word "album"
broadened out into its modern Specification.

misive, and they are OH the permisive
side every time. What is the use of
shade tree laws, if they will not

up. The Supervisors can now take care
OF those roads and plant trees on the
permissive system.

From the Denver Tribune.


strange thing occurred at the City National
Bank, in this city, a few days ago. AS is well
known, this corporation moved into its new
quarters at the corner of 18th and Law
renee streets, quite recently. The vaults there
are new ones, with the latest improved and
combination locks. The officers are thoroughly
familiar with the workings of the locks. but
they being new cannot be held responsible for
any unsatisfactory workings. A few days
ago, when the proper time had ar
rived, an effort was made to unlock
and open the main vault. but after some time
spent in unsuccessfully trying the combination it
was discovered that something was wrong. and
that the bolts held fast where they had been
lodged Meanwhile drafts and checks had been
pouring In, and all the available money had
beenpad out. More were coming in. and inn
mediate action was necessary. telegram " as
at once sent to the vault manufacturers for an
expert to unlock the door, and another tele-
gram explaining the case was sent east for
money. The other banks heard of the circum-
stances and they offered Mr. Hanna all the
money he desired. He gratefully accented
the offer, but afterward found that he had no
use for the loans. For three days the bank
transacted business with its vault doors
closed. and without some Of the books
most used. The strangest part of the
affair was that very few Inconvenience were
felt. During those three days business was
done, aud 1t was on the right side to suit the
circumstances. After paying all the drafts made


upon them the officers Of the bank found that
they had surplus of So, 600 upon their hands
that amount being the sum taken in during the
three days over and above the money paid
The complications in the combination showed
the bank officials that their credit was unlim-
tied, and they have reason to congratulate them
selves upon their lucky escape and financial
standing.


Had the circumstances been different from
what they were no one can tell what the con-
sequences would have been. Had some alarm
list been reused payment and told to call again
the rumor would have gone out that the bank
was in bad way, insolvent, ETC., and an ag-
gravating run would have ensued
